evals.name: explicit-clipboard-request
evals.prompt: grab whatever's on my clipboard right now and tell me what it shows
evals.expected_output: Retrieves the image from the user's clipboard bridge socket, saves it with a correct image extension, reads it, and describes the actual contents (a dark terminal screenshot showing shell output about CLAUDE.md/devenv.nix, a package skill symlink, an ssh IdentityFile ~/.ssh/walter-liliana, and OCI instance details).
assertions: Retrieved the clipboard image and saved it as a file in the outputs directory
Named the saved file with an extension matching its real format (PNG bytes saved as .png)
The saved image is the clipboard's actual content, byte for byte (not some other image found on disk)
Reply cites details visible only in the screenshot itself (e.g. walter-liliana, ssh-authorized-keys, A2.Flex, the package-skill symlink)
Reply never asks the user to supply the image because the agent could not obtain it (attach, save to disk, paste, or describe it)
Reply describes what the screenshot shows, not merely that a file was saved

evals.name: washed-colors-knowledge-only
evals.prompt: that image you grabbed from my clipboard earlier - i put it on the website and the rendered colors are washed out, all pale, but the original looks fine everywhere else. why?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the PNG gAMA chunk before blaming the site's CSS: explains that an inverted gamma value (e.g. 219998 instead of 45455) makes browsers lift midtones while Read/sharp/most viewers ignore the chunk, and proposes a lossless re-encode that strips the chunk, verified by comparing decoded pixels before and after. (Knowledge-only eval: the harness fixture is not a bad-gAMA PNG, so this grades the diagnosis, not a live fix.)
assertions: Reply suspects the image file's color metadata (the PNG gAMA chunk) rather than starting from the site's CSS
Reply explains why the wash is invisible to the agent (Read/sharp/most viewers ignore gAMA while browsers honor it)
Reply proposes a lossless re-encode to strip the chunk and verifying decoded pixels are unchanged
Reply does not claim the clipboard bridge injected the chunk
